messages:
sam: Quick follow-up from today's CP split testing: split-horizon private DNS for tenant endpoints is causing intermittent resolution mismatches across peered VPCs during cutover. Need to decide strategy.

olivia: Can you clarify the mismatch? Is it stale resolver cache in customer VPCs or wrong records in our private hosted zone?

sam: Both. When we flip controlplane region for a tenant we update the private hosted zone in the hosted account. Peered VPCs sometimes still query their VPC-provided resolvers which cache the old A records (TTL 60s) and DNS propagation can be uneven, so some relays route to old endpoints for ~30-120s. That causes short-lived auth failures and misrouted traffic.

priya: Do we use VPC DNS hostnames or do we rely on Route53 resolver inbound endpoints? Which side holds authoritative answers?

sam: Right now the hosted CP writes to a Route53 private hosted zone and we rely on cross-account sharing + peering to allow resolution. Customer side resolver settings vary: some forward to our inbound endpoints, others use native VPC resolver caching.

olivia: Two options: (A) tighten TTL to 5s during cutover and then back to 60s, or (B) implement active DNS handoff with a per-cutover probe that waits for negative-cache flush / validation from peered VPC resolvers before flipping clients. Tradeoffs?

priya: (A) is simple but high query volume and may stress resolver endpoints under mass cutover. (B) is complex but deterministic. There's also (C) serve both endpoints behind a stable VIP (proxy) and move traffic at L4 instead of DNS. That avoids DNS churn entirely but is extra infra.

sam: For (A) we saw that TTL changes don't immediately influence cached entries in some resolvers due to negative caching and local OS resolver behavior. So 5s might not be enough in practice. (B) probe idea: controller pushes new records, then queries a set of representative resolvers in each peered VPC from ephemeral probes until we see the new answer from >=X% of resolvers, then promote.

olivia: That probing sounds better. Need to enumerate representative resolvers: VPC resolver IPs, inbound endpoint IPs, and maybe a small agent in tenant VPC that queries and returns status. For Private deployments customer-managed, we can't run agents, so we'd rely on their inbound endpoints and require they opt-in to the probing flow.

priya: UX: add a per-tenant "dns_handoff_mode" with choices: probe, ttl-leap, vip-proxy. Default: probe for hosted, ttl-leap allowed for low-scale tenants, vip-proxy opt-in for enterprise. Document in onboarding.

netops-bot: netops-bot: Proposed alert rule: "dns_handoff_slow" when probe_completion_time > 120s for >5m. Pager: eng-oncall + neteng.

sam: Implementation sketch for the probe flow: 1) controller creates new record with version tag in TXT: cp-snap-<id>, 2) controller sends resolution probes from regional vantage points and from hosted inbound endpoints into peered VPCs via resolver IPs, 3) each probe returns the A record and TXT tag, 4) controller waits for ack threshold (default 80% of probes) or timeout (default 120s), 5) flip routing and mark rollout step complete.

olivia: Need to be careful with security: the TXT tag in private hosted zones is visible only to resolvers with access; ensure we don't leak any tenant identifiers. Use opaque snapshot hashes not tenant names. Also rotate the probe token per-cutover.

priya: For metricting: dns_probe_success_rate, probe_latency_p95, resolver_hit_rate, stale_records_count. Console should show per-region probe progress in rollout UI and surface a banner if handoff > threshold.

sam: For tenant-managed Private deployments: we add an opt-in small resolver-checker script they can run (shell + awscli) that will respond to our probe via a signed callback. If they opt out, default fallback is TTL-leap but we warn about possible mismatches.

olivia: Edge case: split-horizon with overlapping hostnames where customer also has a local record. We must ensure we don't accidentally override customer-owned entries. Controller should validate ownership via tags or a DNS ownership challenge (create special TXT on their zone).

priya: Good point. Add an ownership verification step: require customer to place a short-lived TXT token at a well-known name or add a tag to their inbound endpoint. This prevents accidental clobber.

sam: Quick troubleshooting snippet we used today to probe resolvers from a lambda container:

```
# dig against VPC resolver
dig @10.0.0.2 tenant-xyz.internal A +short
# verify TXT tag
dig @10.0.0.2 _cp-snap.tenant-xyz.internal TXT +short
```

olivia: We'll need tests: (1) simulate 200 tenant cutovers with mixed resolver topologies and measure probe completion and blackhole incidents, (2) chaos test where some resolvers drop packets to emulate transient failures. If probes fail, controller should abort and rollback to previous records and alert.

netops-bot: netops-bot: Runbook entry proposed: "dns_handoff_probe_playbook". Reference: 1745559999.

priya: Docs/Console work: add a per-cutover timeline view, show probe token, list failure reasons (no-response, stale-cache, ownership-mismatch). Docs to include mitigation steps for customers with aggressive DNS caching (e.g., OS-level caches and embedded devices).

sam: I'll write a short RFC: "split-horizon-dns-handoff-probe" with sequence diagram, probe harness, and rollout checklist. Tagging neteng + devex + security. Aim to spike next sprint.

olivia: Thanks. If RFC lands, devex will mock Console probe UI and docs. Also add a CLI snippet to force re-propagation for a tenant (admin-only).

sam: Will add that. Quick mitigation for impacted customers: enable VIP-proxy for the tenant and coordinate allowlist update, or schedule cutover during maintenance window.

docs: I'll prep draft docs for the three modes and a short troubleshooting checklist.

netops-bot: incident-bot: Note added: "split-horizon DNS mismatch during CP region flip". Reference: 1745559999.
